title: Survey Finds How Holiday Hosting Causes Stress
paragraphs: With Christmas, New Year's and many other winter holidays coming up, a lot of people have plans to host friends and family for festive fun.
However, according to a survey by Talker Research of 2,000 people living in the US, 35% find hosting people during the holidays stressful.
Chores were a major source of stress, with almost half of survey participants saying they spend more time cleaning than actually enjoying their guests' company!

Hosts were found to spend an average of 10 hours cleaning before welcoming people into their homes — and another 10 hours cleaning after they left! This adds up to around two-and-a-half normal workdays just spent cleaning during the holidays.

And hosting comes with many more trade-offs. Fifty-six percent of survey participants said that trying to keep their homes tidy when they had guests made them feel like they were losing quality time with their loved ones, while 36% said they had to sacrifice being able to relax.
The same percentage said cleaning meant they couldn't talk with their guests or enjoy a meal — and none of this is helped by half saying they do all the cleaning themselves.
Getting food ready can also cause a lot of stress, as 41% said they have found themselves still cooking just as guests arrive.
There are ways to lower holiday hosting stress, though. First, you can make and follow a simple plan that gives you lots of time to do everything.
Also, try to get help — rope in others to help with cooking and cleaning, or ask everyone to bring some food and make it a potluck.
Finally, remember that holiday gatherings are about enjoying time together — and you don't need to worry about everything being perfect!
